parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file has one concern: the OrderItem value object in the Order aggregate. The problem is that it enforces its invariants in two different ways. It uses the ddd-lib validator abstraction: addValidators() registers OrderItemQuantityValidator, OrderItemPriceValidator and OrderItemProductValidator into validatorRules. It also hand-codes the same categories of rules in the private static methods validateQuantity and validateProductName, which throw BrokenRulesException directly. Those static checks skip the validator abstraction, so the quantity and product rules live in two places. Inside the file, withQuantity calls validateQuantity and then calls create(), which calls validateQuantity again, so one rule runs twice on the same path. The withIncreasedQuantity increment check is a third inline rule outside the validator mechanism. There are also signs the file has drifted from its own design: it is named *.entity.ts and sits in entities/, but it declares itself a value object (extends DddValueObject), and the doc example calls item.changeQuantity(3), a method that doesn't exist (the real one is withQuantity). The validator classes' contents weren't provided. Their names, and the fact that they are injected with OrderItem, strongly suggest they cover the same quantity and product invariants. That is why confidence is moderate rather than high.

withQuantity() calls validateQuantity and then create(), which validates quantity again, so the rule runs twice. withIncreasedQuantity() adds another inline rule outside validatorRules.
